author: Josemaría Escrivá / Opus Dei
title: Sanctifying with our Work
note: Verified primary (opusdei.org). Fair-use snippet. The core doctrine of the traditionalist pawl: holiness through embedding in ordinary secular institutions.
text: Sanctify your work, sanctify yourself in your work, sanctify others in your work. There is something holy, something divine, hidden in the most ordinary situations, and it is up to each one of you to discover it. It is in the midst of the most material things of the earth that we must sanctify ourselves, serving God and all mankind. The spirit of Opus Dei takes a decided position against having an interior spiritual life and a separate, not spiritual, professional, social, and family life.

author: European Commission
title: The 2022 Code of Practice on Disinformation
note: Verified primary (ec.europa.eu). Fair-use snippet. The contemporary progressive pawl: institutional authority over what counts as true vs 'disinformation'.
text: The Code of Practice on Disinformation is a pioneering framework to address the spread of disinformation, agreed upon by a number of relevant stakeholders. Signatories commit to stronger measures avoiding the placement of advertising next to disinformation, as well as the dissemination of advertising containing disinformation. The Code works towards ensuring fair financial contributions for fact-checkers' work and better access to fact-checkers to information. Users will be better protected from disinformation through enhanced tools to recognise, understand and flag disinformation, to access authoritative sources, and through media literacy initiatives.

author: Marc Andreessen
title: The Techno-Optimist Manifesto
note: Verified primary (a16z.com). Fair-use snippet. The e/acc fork of the utilitarian pawl — risk-calculus flipped to acceleration.
text: We believe technology is a lever on the world, the way to make more with less. We believe there is no material problem that cannot be solved with more technology. We believe free markets are the most effective way to organize a technological economy. We believe in accelerationism, the conscious and deliberate propulsion of technological development. We believe any deceleration of AI will cost lives. We believe we are, have been, and will always be the masters of technology, not mastered by it.

author: Sidney Webb
title: The Labour Party on the Threshold (Fabian Tract No. 207); presidential address to the Labour Party Conference
note: Verified primary work (Fabian Tract 207); text confirmed against multiple sources. Full tract text queued for archive.org fetch (see BACKLOG). The founding technocratic doctrine: gradualness + permeation.
text: Even if we aimed at revolutionising everything at once, we should necessarily be compelled to make each particular change only at the time, and to the extent, and in the manner which ten or fifteen million electors could be brought to consent to it. This is the inevitability of gradualness. Most reformers think that all they have got to do in a political democracy is to obtain a majority. This is a profound mistake. What has to be changed is not only the vote that is cast, but also the mental climate in which Parliament and the Government both live and work.

author: Mark Carney / Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero
title: Amount of finance committed to achieving 1.5C now at scale needed to deliver the transition
note: Verified primary (gfanzero.com press release, COP26). Fair-use snippet. The green pawl at central-bank/asset-manager scale — building the disclosure infrastructure.
text: Over 130 trillion dollars of private capital is committed to transforming the economy for net zero. To support the deployment of this capital, the global financial system is being transformed through 24 major initiatives. The architecture of the global financial system has been transformed to deliver net zero. We now have the essential plumbing in place to move climate change from the fringes to the forefront of finance so that every financial decision takes climate change into account.
